title: Proactive Stabilization and Warm-Handoff Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook documents the proactive incident-avoidance workflow and a standardized warm-handoff procedure for operators managing Redwood Inference serving services. It covers monitoring triggers, pre-incident mitigation steps, automated remediation, manual escalation paths, warm-handoff checklist, customer-signal templates for status pages and CSRs, and a post-event debrief template. The goal is to detect and stabilize degradations before they become customer-impacting incidents and to ensure handoffs are smooth and information-rich when escalation is required.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: inference fronting proxies, routing layer, runtime pods, KV cache, batching controller, model-serving workers, and serving control plane.
- Not covered: billing pipelines, onboarding identity flows (see separate billing and identity runbooks).

Goals and success metrics:
- Detect 80% of actionable regressions inside the detection window (3min for latency spikes, 10min for throughput anomalies).
- Keep customer-visible error rate < 0.1% and P95 latency under SLO during transient degradations via automatic fallback.
- Average handoff documentation time < 5 minutes for operator->oncall.

Definitions and severity mapping:
- Severity A (sev-1): Service outage, >50% tenant errors, or SLO breach with >5min customer-visible disruption.
- Severity B (sev-2): Significant degradation (P95 > 2x baseline or sustained token throughput reduction >30%) with limited customer impact.
- Severity C (sev-3): Internal-only regressions, alerting noise, or emerging anomalies requiring investigation.

Monitoring triggers (examples):
- Latency:P95 > 2x baseline for >2 consecutive minutes across >=2 regions.
- Errors: 5xx rate > 0.5% over 5 minutes and increase >300% vs rolling 24h baseline.
- Throughput: sustained backlog > 150% capacity of active GPU pool for 10 minutes.
- Cache: KV cache eviction rate > 10% per minute or miss-rate jump >50%.
- Autoscaler signals: repeated scale-up failures or OOM kill frequency > 3/hour.

Automated (pre-manual) remediation chain:
1) Circuit breaker: automatically route new requests to fallback model variant when error rate threshold hit.
2) Short-term autoscale: burst up to 30% extra capacity for 10 minutes if queue growth detected.
3) Prefix/KV cache warm-up: replay hot prefixes from recent traces to rebuild caches.
4) Rate-limit soft-fallthrough: reduce per-tenant token limits by 20% to protect global SLOs.

When to invoke a manual incident:
1) Any Sev-A trigger fires.
2) If automated remediation does not reduce customer-visible error rate below 0.1% within 5 minutes.
3) Repeated autoscaler failures or infrastructure health signals (OOM on >2 nodes) persist for >10 minutes.

Operator first-response checklist (10-minute stabilization script):
1) Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and create/attach timeline in the incident tracker.
2) Identify impacted service(s) and region(s).
3) Run quick health queries:
   - curl -s "https://ops-api.internal/health?service=serving" | jq .status
   - redis-cli INFO | grep evicted_keys
   - kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide | grep CrashLoopBackOff
4) If cache miss/eviction spike: invoke cache-warm command: opsctl cache warm --service serving --window 15m
5) If backlog spike: trigger short-term autoscale: opsctl autoscale request --service serving --scale-by 30 --duration 10m
6) Apply temporary routing fallback: opsctl route set --service serving --variant fallback-small --percent 100 --until now+15m
7) Notify stakeholders using the Incident Bridge template (see Customer & Exec comms).
8) Start evidence collection: collect traces (last 30m), pprof, kernel logs, and heap dumps where relevant.

Warm-handoff protocol (operator -> oncall or cross-team):
Required conditions to perform a warm-handoff:
- Operator has attempted automated remediation steps (above) and impact remains or further investigation is required.
- Handoff should occur within the same PagerDuty incident number; do not open separate incidents for the same problem.

Warm-handoff steps (fill and paste into the bridge chat):
1) Situation summary (2 sentences): what, where, when started, current impact.
2) Actions taken: list commands run and automated steps invoked, with timestamps.
3) Evidence links: traces, logs, dashboards, and key alerts with direct URLs.
4) Hypotheses: short bullet list of current working theories.
5) Next recommended action(s) and owner(s) with estimated time to complete.
6) Known constraints: deploy freeze windows, maintenance events, or cross-team dependencies.
7) Contact info: primary operator, backup, and escalation owner (Slack handles).

Example warm-handoff script (copy/paste):
---
Situation: P95 latency in us-west-2 increased from 120ms to 520ms starting 2026-02-02T09:12Z; approx 12% of requests returned 502.
Actions: Applied fallback routing to fallback-small at 09:18Z; autoscale request +30% at 09:19Z; cache warm-up at 09:21Z.
Evidence: dashboards/redwood/serving/us-west-2?from=09:00Z, traces/redwood/serving/trace-id=abc123, logs: s3://ops-evidence/serving/2026-02-02/us-west-2.zip
Hypotheses: 1) new kernel version on gpu nodes introduced driver regression; 2) batch scheduler mis-calculated sequence lengths causing OOM.
Next steps: (1) Oncall: validate node driver health (owner: @sofia) within 10m; (2) Platform: roll back kernel on suspected node group if confirmed (owner: @marcus).
Constraints: Can only rollback nodegroup-2 between 09:30-09:45Z due to maintenance window.
Contact: @aisha (operator), @sofia (oncall), PagerDuty#12345.
---

Incident bridge and communication templates:
- Internal bridge join message (short):
   "Joining incident PD#12345 — service=serving, region=us-west-2, impact=latency/p95 520ms, operator=aisha, current actions: fallback routing, autoscale. Evidence: <link>"
- Customer-facing status page template (short window):
   Title: "Partial service degradation in US-West (latency) — investigating"
   Body: "We are currently investigating increased latency for inference requests in our US-West region. Some requests may experience delays or transient errors. Our engineers have applied a temporary routing fallback and are actively stabilizing the service. We will post an update within 30 minutes or sooner. Customer impact: intermittent increased latency and occasional 502 responses."
- Customer-facing status page template (extended incident):
   Title: "Service disruption affecting inference requests — US and APAC"
   Body: "We are experiencing a broader disruption affecting inference request latency and errors across multiple regions. Our on-call and platform engineers are engaged and performing targeted mitigations including autoscaling, cache warm-up, and controlled rollbacks where required. We will update every 60 minutes until service is restored. If you are experiencing critical production impact, please open a support ticket referencing incident PD#12345."

Escalation matrix (condensed):
- Operator -> Oncall (SRE): immediate (PagerDuty)
- Oncall -> Platform GPU team: if infrastructure signal present or OOMs detected
- Oncall -> Eng serving-runtime: if kernel/scheduler or model-serving worker behavior suspected
- Oncall -> Customer Success: if customer-facing credit/communication required

Roles & ownership conventions:
- Incident Commander (IC): owns coordination, public comms, and bridge timeline. Default is the oncall SRE for Sev-A/B incidents.
- Technical Lead: owns triage of technical hypotheses and directs rollbacks/config changes.
- Evidence Engineer: collects and stores forensic artifacts and ensures regulatory retention for enterprise customers.

Game day & proactive simulation guidance:
- Bi-weekly simulation: dedicated 90-minute sessions focusing on cache-eviction and batching failures.
- Scenario example: simulate a KV cache loss in one region; expected outcome: automatic fallback routes, cache warm replay, and recovery in <12 minutes.
- Scoring rubric: time to first mitigation <5m (10 pts), time to stable <12m (20 pts), handoff clarity score by reviewer >8/10 (10 pts).

Runbook primitives (commands & endpoints):
- opsctl service status --service serving --region us-west-2
- opsctl logs tail --service serving --since 15m --filter "error OR OOM"
- opsctl route set --service serving --variant fallback-small --percent 100 --until now+15m
- opsctl cache warm --service serving --window 15m
- opsctl evidence collect --incident PD12345 --output s3://ops-evidence/serving/PD12345.zip

Evidence retention policy (short):
- Critical incidents (Sev-A): retain full forensic bundle for 2 years.
- Non-critical incidents (Sev-B/C): retain artifacts for 90 days.

Post-incident debrief template (to be filled within 72h):
1) Incident summary (what happened and timeline).
2) Root cause(s) (confirmed and unconfirmed hypotheses).
3) Workarounds and mitigations applied.
4) Actions taken and owners (include PR/CL links).
5) Action items with due dates and measured risk reduction.
6) Postmortem severity and customer impact assessment.
7) Lessons learned and monitoring improvements.

Operational run cadence & ownership for the playbook:
- Playbook owner: Eng SRE (primary: Marcus Lee).
- Quarterly review: playbook and thresholds reviewed by SRE and Serving Runtime teams.
- Game day owner: Eng SRE rotations coordinator (Sofia Martinez).

Appendix A — Example packet of evidence to collect:
- kube events and pod manifests (kubectl -n serving get events --all-namespaces)
- pprof CPU/mem profiles for worker processes
- last 1 hour application traces (jaeger or opentelemetry) filtered by trace sampling ids
- exact CLI command history from remediation steps (opsctl logs)
- node-level dmesg and driver logs for GPU nodes

Appendix B — Template for customer support reply (short):
"Thanks for the report — we are aware of elevated latency in <region>. Our engineers are actively mitigating; we have applied temporary routing fallbacks and expect reduced impact within 30–60 minutes. We will follow up when service is fully restored. Incident reference: PD#12345." 

Appendix C — Runbook change log:
- 2026-01-15: initial published playbook (Aisha Patel).
- 2026-02-02: clarified warm-handoff template and added cache-warm primitive (reviewers: Marcus Lee, Sofia Martinez).

For questions or to propose edits, ping #eng-sre-playbooks on Slack or email playbooks@redwood.example.com.
